newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government against rejoining NATO.
newsitem.headline: French government against rejoining NATO.

text.p: The French left-wing government said on Friday that conditions were not ripe for France to return to the military wing of NATO, but it was up to conservative President Jacques Chirac to decide whether to pursue moves to rejoin.

"Regarding France and NATO, the president of the Republic has taken the initiative of a rapprochement...Without prejudging the president's assessment, conditions set to pursue the process do not seem to be fulfilled," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rumelhardt said.
Rummelhardt told a news briefing that Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin would not attend next month's NATO summit in Madrid, where France will be represented by Chirac.
"But the issues to be debated there concern both the president and the prime minister," he said.
"It is natural that (Chirac) assess himself whether he should go further in that direction (of a rapprochement)," he said.

France, which pulled out of NATO's military wing in 1966 under General Charles de Gaulle, has set as a condition for rejoining that the United States relinquish NATO's Naples-based southern command to a European officer. Washington, which also runs NATO's supreme command, has rejected the French condition.
